contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0001 (stack-versus-space conventions) and with the packet's C66-GEO-COMP demand for components, stabilizers, and finite-cover behaviour of Z. INDEPENDENT DERIVATION. ATT-0096 clause (2)/CLM-0096-2 takes V to be a connected normal component of the distinct-support open U of the Abel–Jacobi incidence over the reduced balanced normalized Hurwitz stack H, then argues: étale monodromy through H_V⊂S_6 has [S_6:H_V] orbits of size |H_V|; a finite étale cover of a normal scheme is normal; irreducible components of a locally Noetherian normal scheme are open and closed; hence those orbits are the irreducible components, each of degree |H_V|. The cited facts are scheme-scoped. Stacks 58.7 (03SF) transfers the Galois-category language to finite étale morphisms of connected schemes. Stacks Lemma 58.11.2 (0BQL) says that a connected finite étale cover of a normal integral scheme is itself an integral normal scheme. Stacks Lemma 28.7.7 (033N) says a locally Noetherian scheme is normal if and only if it is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes. None of these tags applies to an algebraic stack. Normality of a stack is the smooth-atlas property: Stacks 100.7 (04YE) and Remark 100.7.3 (04YH) make 'normal' a smooth-local scheme property, so a stack is normal precisely when some (equivalently any) smooth atlas is a normal scheme. Étale morphisms of stacks are a separate, DM-restricted notion (Stacks 101.35/0CIK): they are not 'smooth of relative dimension 0', and the residual-gerbe examples [A^1/G_m] and [Spec k/μ_p] show that stacky finite/quasi-finite behaviour is not the scheme one. Residual gerbes exist under the Stacks 100.11 (06ML) hypotheses; their automorphism groups are the geometric inertia. Noohi (arXiv math/0201021v1, Thm 1.1) puts a homomorphism ω_x from Aut of the residue gerbe into π_1 of the stack, and identifies π_1(stack)/N with π_1 of the coarse space, N being generated by all such inertia images. Consequently inertia acts on the geometric fibre of a finite étale cover, in particular on the ordered S_6-fibre. If H_V is computed from coarse-space or atlas path monodromy without that groupoid/inertia action, the orbit count and the degrees need not match the irreducible components or representable degrees of the stack Z_V. Noohi moreover defines a covering space of a stack to be a finite étale representable morphism, so representability is an extra datum, not a formal consequence of writing 'S_6-torsor' in scheme language. The finding's rescue clauses are exactly the ones these sources license: (i) inertia-free, i.e. I_V→V an equivalence, so V is an algebraic space (Stacks Prop. 94.13.3/04SZ) and one reduces to FND-0132; or (ii) pull back to a normal scheme atlas, apply 03SF+0BQL+033N there, and descend along R=U×_V U while tracking how residual-gerbe automorphisms permute components. A third, equivalent, route is to take H_V as the image of the stacky π_1 so that inertia is already inside the monodromy; ATT-0096 does not do this. SCOPE SHARPENING. The finding is a proof-obligation obstruction, not a numerical counterexample: it does not assert that [S_6:H_V] fails when H_V is the stacky monodromy image and components/degrees are those of the stack. It asserts that the scheme-theoretic formula, as written and as used in CLM-0096-2, is not valid on a stack without one of the extra hypotheses. RELATION TO THE CORPUS. Complementary to corroborated FND-0132 (FAUD-0137 scoped the connected-to-irreducible upgrade to a connected locally Noetherian scheme; the missing piece here is stackiness/inertia, not normality). Complementary to FND-0127 (scheme-to-stack descent for Grauert/Abel–Jacobi identifications, not Galois component counts). Complementary to FND-0064 (existence of the stack-level S_6-torsor on pairwise-distinct sections) and FND-0075 (that torsor fails on coarse moduli when automorphisms permute marks; Q-coefficient cohomology descent is harmless, which does not salvage an integral/scheme-theoretic component-and-degree formula). Complementary to FND-0137 (which Aut group appears in the forgetful inertia sequence for u:Z→M_{6,6}). Distinct from all of the above: do not merge. Kind 'obstruction' is correct for CLM-0096-2. Merge target: none. Promote candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source. The finding's sole reviewer_engine (qwen) is in this revision's excluded_engines; this audit is the first non-excluded verification.

scope.exact_mathematical_scope: If Z_V→V is a finite étale S_6-ordering cover (equivalently, the restriction of a stack-level S_6-torsor of orderings of the reduced-support open) over a connected normal algebraic stack V, the scheme-theoretic formula 'Z_V has [S_6:H_V] irreducible components, each finite étale of degree |H_V|' is not a theorem of the scheme Galois correspondence. That formula is licensed by Stacks 03SF/0BQL/033N only when V is a connected normal locally Noetherian scheme (or, after 04SZ, an algebraic space, equivalently I_V→V an equivalence). Over a stack it becomes valid only after one of: (i) an inertia-free/representability hypothesis reducing to that scheme case; (ii) descent to a normal scheme atlas, applying the scheme lemmas there, then tracking how the groupoid R=U×_V U, including residual-gerbe automorphisms, permutes components and degrees; or (iii) a stacky π_1 Galois correspondence in which H_V is the image of π_1^ét(V) (Noohi), so that inertia is already inside the monodromy. In the campaign, V is a connected normal component of the distinct-support Abel–Jacobi open U over the reduced balanced normalized Hurwitz stack, so the scheme lemmas do not apply as written to CLM-0096-2.
excluded_claims: Does not assert that the numerical count is false when H_V is the image of the stacky étale fundamental group and components/degrees are those of the stack Z_V.
